def: The lower or lowest side of anything. Paley.
The quality of being impressible; susceptibility.
Having the character of larceny; as, a larcenous act;committing larceny. "The larcenous and burglarious world." SydneySmith.-- Lar"ce*nous*ly, adv.
A woman who officiated in sacred rites among pagans. Abp.Potter.
Having the quality or power of conducting; as, the conductivetissue of a pistil.The ovarian walls . . . are seen to be distinctly conductive. Goodale(Gray's Bot. ).
To adorn with spangles; to dot or sprinkle with somethingbrilliant or glittering.The grass . . . is all bespangled with dewdrops. Cowper.
A place for dregs and dirt; a sink; a sewer. [Obs.] Latimer.
A jet of steam issuing from a fissure in the earth.
A firing in the direction of the length of a trench, or a lineof parapet or troops, etc.; a raking fire.

A tumor of fleshy consistence; -- formerly applied to manyvarieties of tumor, now restricted to a variety of malignant growthmade up of cells resembling those of fetal development without anyproper intercellular substance.
A kind of aboriginal shell money, or wampum, of the Atlanticcoast of the United States; -- originally applied only to polishedwhite cylindrical beads.
